task.name: A story gate returned PASS for a commit that fails the identical gate on the merge base it produced
task.story_text:
## Observed

In the hdp adopter repo, commit `71ac67f6` was developed and reviewed under a
forge story and its gate returned PASS. It was merged. The next sprint
(`issues-337,339,340`, run `a0b1e4fd770b`) terminated before any dev work
started:

```
RuntimeError: Broken baseline: configured gate failed on sprint merge base
544e476c005235279c93d73ee47d8965cbf2af8e before any dev work started
(Gate returned FAIL) (failure reproduced on an immediate re-run of the
identical gate)
```

The five failing tests were the five that `71ac67f6` had introduced. Each
raised `FileNotFoundError` on `hdp_mcp/resources/schema_tables.json`, a
gitignored generated file, and each passes whenever that file happens to be
present on disk.

The adopter-side test defect that made those tests environment-dependent is
fixed and merged as hdp#343. What is still unexplained is the PASS: the story's
own gate covered the same tests on the same code and did not fail, so that gate
either ran against a tree that carried the gitignored file or did not run those
tests at all.

Two candidate explanations belong to forge rather than to the adopter, and
neither has been examined. The first is whether the story's worktree was in fact
freshly created, since a fresh git worktree does not inherit ignored files and
nothing in the adopter's own test suite writes to that directory (every
`server.get_tables()` call site patches `server.RESOURCES_DIR`, and `hdp_mcp` is
not an installed package, so the path resolves inside the worktree rather than
into site-packages). The second is whether the story gate and the baseline gate
ran the same test selection at all: hdp's configured gate command is
`make forge-gate TEST_TARGET={test_target}`, so the two verdicts are only
comparable if the same target was substituted into both, and the run record has
not been checked for what was actually substituted.

## Expected

A gate verdict is a claim about a commit, so it should hold for that commit
wherever the same gate is run. When forge records PASS for a change and that
change is merged, the base that results should not fail the identical gate.
Where a verdict can turn on state outside the commit — files present in the
working tree that the commit does not carry, or a narrower test selection than
the one the next consumer of that base will run — that dependence should be
visible in the recorded gate result at the time the verdict is issued, rather
than being discovered later by the run that inherits the base. An operator
reading a recorded PASS should be able to tell what was executed and against
what tree state, so that a green verdict distinguishes a change that is safe to
build on from a condition local to the environment the gate happened to run in.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `995bb31885eec37019a58bc0c3dcef02451aea06` captured at `2026-08-20T22:19:15.512062+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `/Users/pwickersham/src/hdp/hdp_mcp/resources/schema_tables.json` — `sha256:3459c9d684930ba60ca99cdd6000385e63e1760d698dc0fc059729710eefabd6`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py` — `sha256:9c5ed787de305cccfaf0be7043a5e46d33aae7d1dc98f2edc57bc9609516d2ae`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:b96b51ac6bf64a7e254e56f89c2524a8fa9c495f5177aa2fd547d60dca4fa42d`

### Observed symptom

A story's own forge gate (running `make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.`) returned PASS
for commit 71ac67f6 in the hdp adopter repo. That commit was merged. The very
next sprint's baseline gate — the identical command run against the resulting
merge base 544e476c — FAILED, on the exact five tests the merged commit had
introduced, each raising FileNotFoundError for the gitignored
hdp_mcp/resources/schema_tables.json. The divergence is not explained by a test
selection difference (both gates substituted the same TEST_TARGET) — it is
explained by which physical worktree each gate ran in and whether that
worktree could have accumulated a leftover gitignored artifact.

### Reproduction / evidence

hdp .forge/audits/runs/13a56e534cb5.json (story issue-340, commit 71ac67f6):
validation_runs shows `command: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.`, `result: PASS`,
workspace.path = /Users/pwickersham/src/hdp/.forge/worktrees/issue-340.

hdp .forge/audits/run-a0b1e4fd770b-sprint-audit.yaml: baseline_check for the
next sprint used the identical `command: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.` against
merge_base 544e476c, `decision: FAIL`, failing the five
tests/test_hdp_mcp_live_surface.py tests with FileNotFoundError, worktree
/Users/pwickersham/src/hdp/.forge/forge-baseline-r1rvxpeu/worktree.

Same command substitution on both sides rules out a TEST_TARGET mismatch — the
Makefile (hdp Makefile:380-383) normalizes both "." and "{test_target}" to
`pytest tests/`, so both gates ran the full suite.

hdp_mcp/schema_gen.py:36 (`RESOURCES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "resources"`)
makes the resources path resolve relative to whatever checkout hdp_mcp is
imported from — i.e. per-worktree, not shared via any installed package
(hdp_mcp is not declared under pyproject.toml's `packages`).
hdp_mcp/server.py:116-120 `get_tables()` calls the *real*, unpatched
`generate_if_stale()` and then reads `RESOURCES_DIR / "schema_tables.json"`
whenever it is invoked outside the test's own monkeypatch — so any real
(non-test) invocation of `get_tables()`/`generate_if_stale()` during dev work
in a worktree legitimately writes that gitignored file into that worktree's
own hdp_mcp/resources/ for real.

theforge src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:619-651 `_is_stale_worktree`:
a worktree with commits ahead of base_branch is NOT stale and is reused as-is
(line 1266 `"↻ WORKSPACE  reusing existing worktree"`). The reuse path
(lines 1266-1289) runs setup_command and `_deindex_forge_artifacts(...,
purge=True)` (workspace.py:843-850), but that function only
`git rm --cached`/deletes a fixed list `_FORGE_ARTIFACTS` of forge-internal
files — it never runs `git clean` or otherwise removes arbitrary
untracked/gitignored files elsewhere in the tree. No call to `git clean`
exists anywhere in workspace.py. So a worktree that is reused across a
story's dev iterations keeps any gitignored file any process wrote into it
at any point in its history.

theforge src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1209 (`temp_root =
Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=BASELINE_TEMP_PREFIX, dir=forge_temp_root))`) and
:1227 (`git worktree add --detach <temp_root>/worktree <merge_base_ref>`):
the baseline gate for the *next* sprint always creates a brand-new temp
directory and a brand-new detached worktree — it is structurally impossible
for it to inherit any leftover file from a story worktree.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The story's gate and the baseline gate ran different test selections (TEST_TARGET substitution mismatch), so the story's gate simply never exercised the five failing tests.
  - Evidence: Both validation_runs entries record the identical command `make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.`, and hdp's Makefile (line 380-383) normalizes both "." and the unfilled "{test_target}" template to the same `pytest tests/` invocation — so both gates ran the full suite, including the five tests in question.
- **[confirmed]** forge's story worktree was never freshly created for this story, or is reused/persisted across dev iterations without cleaning untracked/gitignored files, so a real (non-test) invocation of get_tables()/generate_if_stale() during earlier dev work in that same worktree legitimately wrote hdp_mcp/resources/schema_tables.json to disk, and it then silently masked the test's monkeypatch bug for every later gate run in that worktree — while the next sprint's baseline gate, which always builds a brand-new temp worktree, could never have that file and failed for real.
  - Evidence: workspace.py's `_is_stale_worktree` (line 619) preserves any worktree with commits ahead of base_branch — it is reused (line 1266), not recreated. The reuse path's only untracked-file cleanup is `_deindex_forge_artifacts` (line 843), which is scoped to a fixed list of forge-internal artifacts and never runs `git clean` on the rest of the tree — no `git clean` call exists anywhere in the file. Meanwhile `_run_baseline_gate` (runner.py:1209, 1227) allocates a brand-new `tempfile.mkdtemp` directory and a fresh `git worktree add --detach` for every single run, so it structurally cannot inherit anything from a story worktree. hdp_mcp/server.py's `get_tables()` (server.py:116-120) calls the real `generate_if_stale()` and writes to the per-worktree `RESOURCES_DIR` (schema_gen.py:36, `Path(__file__).parent / "resources"`) whenever invoked outside a test's monkeypatch — exactly the kind of write that, once made in a worktree that forge never cleans on reuse, persists for every subsequent gate run of that same story.

### Confirmed cause

forge's worktree lifecycle treats a story worktree with committed work as
reusable across the story's dev/review/gate iterations (workspace.py
`_is_stale_worktree` + the reuse branch at workspace.py:1266-1289) and never
cleans untracked/gitignored files from it on reuse — the only cleanup,
`_deindex_forge_artifacts`, is scoped to a fixed list of forge-internal
artifacts, not the general tree. This means any gitignored file that gets
written into a story worktree at any point during that story's lifecycle
(here, hdp_mcp/resources/schema_tables.json, written by a real,
non-test-mocked invocation of hdp_mcp's `get_tables()`/`generate_if_stale()`
during dev work) remains present for every later gate run against that same
worktree, including the merge-authority gate that decided PASS. The next
sprint's baseline gate, by contrast, always allocates a brand-new
`tempfile.mkdtemp` directory and a fresh `git worktree add --detach` off the
merge base (runner.py:1209/1227), so it never carries that leftover file and
fails on the same commit. The recorded PASS therefore reflected worktree
state the merged commit did not itself carry, and that dependency was not
visible anywhere in the recorded gate result.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py: `_is_stale_worktree` (line 619) and the
worktree-reuse branches (lines ~1257-1289, ~1309-1334, ~1339-1375), plus
`_deindex_forge_artifacts` (line 843) whose cleanup scope is limited to
`_FORGE_ARTIFACTS` rather than the worktree's full untracked/ignored state.

### Fix-success criterion

A story worktree that is reused across dev iterations (commits-ahead, not
stale) has its gate run against a tree state equivalent to a fresh checkout
of the same commit for the purpose of untracked/gitignored files — either by
cleaning untracked files before each gate invocation that decides PASS/FAIL,
or by recording in the gate result which untracked/gitignored paths were
present in the worktree at gate time, so a PASS verdict is falsifiable
against the same commit run in a truly clean tree. Concretely: reproducing
this scenario (a project whose tests read a real, gitignored, generated
artifact without full monkeypatch coverage) no longer produces a story-gate
PASS that a fresh-worktree baseline gate on the resulting merge base
contradicts.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- hdp_mcp/server.py's get_tables()/get_relationships()/get_examples() import RESOURCES_DIR by name from schema_gen at module-load time, so a test that only monkeypatches schema_gen.RESOURCES_DIR does not redirect what server.py reads — this is the adopter-side test defect, already diagnosed and fixed as hdp#343 (branch fix/mcp-live-surface-resources-dir, commit 858ec73a); it is the trigger for the divergent verdicts but not itself a forge defect. (related: hdp#343)
- forge's worktree-reuse path has no general untracked/gitignored-file cleanup step at all (only a fixed forge-internal artifact list is purged); this is a broader gap than just this one story — any adopter test suite that writes real, gitignored generated artifacts as a side effect of non-test code paths run during dev iterations is exposed to the same PASS-on-stale-state / FAIL-on-fresh-base divergence, independent of the specific hdp bug.

### Notes

This diagnosis resolves the "process-level question" left open (status:
inconclusive) by the adopter-side diagnosis at
/Users/pwickersham/src/hdp/.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-342-5b6b86a15eb8.yaml,
which independently confirmed the test-level root cause (an import-time
RESOURCES_DIR aliasing bug in hdp_mcp/server.py, already fixed as hdp#343) but
explicitly declined to establish why the story's own gate worktree carried a
real schema_tables.json.

I could not directly inspect the issue-340 worktree's contents at the moment
its gate ran PASS — the worktree directory (.forge/worktrees/issue-340 in the
hdp repo) was already cleaned up by the time of this investigation (worktrees
dir is now empty), and no reused-worktree state is captured in the run audit.
The confirmed cause rests on: (a) the code-level mechanism that make a real
get_tables() call write the gitignored file into a per-worktree path, (b) the
confirmed absence of any cleanup of arbitrary untracked files on forge's
worktree-reuse path, and (c) the confirmed freshness of the baseline gate's
worktree on every run. I did not find a log line proving a real
get_tables()/generate_if_stale() call actually fired during issue-340's dev
iterations (dev_verification_requests in the run audit is empty, and no
application code outside test files calls generate_if_stale()) — this is the
one remaining gap, noted rather than papered over. The structural
cause (reused worktrees are not cleaned of untracked files while baseline
worktrees always are) holds regardless of the precise write's origin, and is
what the fix should target: the gate's tree-state guarantee, not the specific
write site.

ac_verification.criterion: Symptom resolution: A story gate returned PASS for a commit that failed the identical gate on the merge base it produced.
ac_verification.evidence: src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:57 captures untracked and ignored paths with git status immediately before the gate command runs, src/theforge/coordinator/validate_phase.py:840 and src/theforge/coordinator/validate_phase.py:855 propagate that snapshot into recorded validation runs, src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1308 and src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1338 persist the same state for baseline gates, and src/theforge/cli/audit.py:182 renders validation worktree_state for operators. tests/test_validation_profile_seam.py:117 verifies story validation records carry gate-time untracked and ignored residue, tests/test_sprint_baseline_gate.py:152 verifies a real git baseline worktree records an ignored generated path, and tests/test_cli_audit.py:13 verifies the recorded state is visible in audit output.

ac_verification.criterion: A story worktree that is reused across dev iterations (commits-ahead, not stale) has its gate run against a tree state equivalent to a fresh checkout of the same commit for the purpose of untracked/gitignored files — either by cleaning untracked files before each gate invocation that decides PASS/FAIL, or by recording in the gate result which untracked/gitignored paths were present in the worktree at gate time, so a PASS verdict is falsifiable against the same commit run in a truly clean tree.
ac_verification.evidence: The spec offers a disjunction and the recording branch is implemented. src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py lines 57-96 add _snapshot_gate_worktree_state, running git status --porcelain=v1 --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all in the gate's own workspace, splitting results into untracked and ignored, dropping forge-owned .forge/ entries, and recording capture_error rather than failing the gate when the inspection itself fails; gate.py line 236 invokes it immediately before the gate command and hands the value out through worktree_state_out. validate_phase.py lines 846-860 and 902-915 thread it into _record_gate_run / _record_gate_commit / _record_validation_run and on into validation_profiles.validation_run_record (lines 219-246), and the _gate_worktree_state.clear() at line 895 keeps the advisory run's residue out of the widened merge-authority verdict. The recorded runs reach the persisted audit (coordinator/audit.py line 803) and survive resume (run_setup.py lines 252-255), and this cycle adds the operator view: cli/audit.py lines 27-50 plus the print at line 194 render the residue directly under the validation entry. Tests: tests/test_coord_gate_exec.py TestSnapshotGateWorktreeState covers the parse and the capture-error-without-blocking path; tests/test_validation_profile_seam.py test_the_recorded_verdict_carries_gate_time_worktree_state drives a full run_task across the phase boundary and asserts the non-skipped merge-authority record carries the residue; tests/test_cli_audit.py test_cmd_audit_renders_validation_worktree_state asserts the rendered line. I ran these files plus test_sprint_baseline_gate.py and test_coord_workspace_merge.py: 82 passed.

ac_verification.criterion: Concretely: reproducing this scenario (a project whose tests read a real, gitignored, generated artifact without full monkeypatch coverage) no longer produces a story-gate PASS that a fresh-worktree baseline gate on the resulting merge base contradicts.
ac_verification.evidence: Under the recording branch the spec's Expected section asks that the dependence be visible in the recorded gate result at the time the verdict is issued, and both sides of the hdp divergence now carry it. Story side: validate_phase.py lines 846-860 and 902-915 attach the snapshot to the merge-authority record. Baseline side: sprint/runner.py line 1313 passes worktree_state_out into the baseline gate and lines 1338, 1365, 1405, 1451 and 1536 write worktree_state onto the pass record, the initial_result, the confirmation_result, the not-reproduced record and the reproduced-failure record; lines 1462-1467 reassign decision, output_tail and resolved_gate_cmd to the confirmation values before that final record is built, so the confirm_worktree_state used at line 1536 belongs to the same run as the verdict beside it while the first run's state is preserved separately under initial_result. This cycle closes the coverage gap that mattered for the hdp symptom: tests/test_sprint_baseline_gate.py _init_repo now commits a 'generated/' ignore rule and test_baseline_gate_records_gate_time_worktree_state writes both an untracked build/cache.txt and a gitignored generated/cache.txt into a real git baseline worktree, asserting the record captures untracked=['build/cache.txt'] and ignored=['generated/'] — the actual git invocation and its ignored-mode behaviour, not a stubbed transcript. A gate verdict issued in a tree carrying a generated file the commit does not carry is therefore falsifiable from its own record, and visible to an operator through forge audit.

finding_registry.description: The audit renderer prints each validation run's profile, authority, result and command but omits the newly recorded gate-time worktree_state, so an operator reading a recorded PASS through the audit command still sees no sign that the verdict was produced in a worktree carrying untracked or ignored residue.

The only test that exercises the residue snapshot against a real git repository produces an untracked file, while every assertion about the ignored list is made against a stubbed git status string, so the ignored-path behaviour of the actual command that was chosen is never executed by the suite.

The iteration landed as a commit whose subject line is the literal text 'acceptance_criteria:', while the accompanying handoff reports an empty commits list and states the commit could not be created at all, so the branch history and the structured handoff disagree about what was delivered and the log entry does not name the change.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
